canonical_statement: The primary objective was to evaluate virological outcomes on B/F/TAF according to pre-existing resistance mutations and baseline plasma HIV-1 RNA.

Secondary objectives were to identify factors associated with virological failure, describe emergence of resistance at failure by baseline viral-load group, and describe long-term follow-up of suppressed and unsuppressed groups.
The study was a retrospective analysis within the prospective ANRS-CO3-AquiVIH-NA cohort, which follows people with HIV at 15 hospitals in southwestern France.

canonical_statement: Participants were treatment-experienced people with HIV who initiated B/F/TAF during 2018–2021.
Participants were classified as virologically suppressed when baseline plasma HIV-1 RNA was <50 copies/mL and virologically unsuppressed when it was >50 copies/mL.

population.label: B/F/TAF-treated participants classified by baseline plasma HIV-1 RNA

canonical_statement: Virological failure was defined as two consecutive plasma HIV-1 RNA measurements >50 and <1000 copies/mL or a single measurement >1000 copies/mL within 60 months; for participants starting B/F/TAF with plasma HIV-1 RNA >50 copies/mL, failure also included absence of a value <50 copies/mL during the first 12 months.

outcome.definition: Two consecutive pVL >50 and <1000 copies/mL, or one pVL >1000 copies/mL within 60 months; for baseline pVL >50, no pVL <50 within 12 months also counted as failure.

canonical_statement: Genotypic resistance tests were performed using Sanger sequencing, and resistance-associated mutations were interpreted using version 34 of the ANRS resistance algorithm.

Pre-existing NRTI and INSTI resistance was assessed cumulatively from all available pre-B/F/TAF RNA or DNA genotypic resistance tests; APOBEC-associated mutations were excluded when proviral DNA sequences were hypermutated or contained stop codons.

The genotypic susceptibility score was the sum of fully active B/F/TAF components; bictegravir was assumed fully active when baseline integrase genotype was unavailable and no previous virological failure on an INSTI regimen was documented.

Group comparisons used chi-square or Fisher exact tests; Aalen–Johansen curves estimated virological-failure probability with competing censoring, and Cox proportional hazards models were used to identify factors associated with virological failure.
Of 1430 cohort participants who started B/F/TAF during 2018–2021, 636 had available genotypic resistance-test results and comprised the analyzed genotyped population.

canonical_statement: Participants without any genotypic resistance data were excluded, so the overall prevalence of pre-existing resistance mutations may have been underestimated.
Some suppressed participants had only proviral DNA genotyping, whose limited sensitivity could have missed NRTI pre-existing resistance mutations.

Emerging resistance could have been underestimated because genotypic resistance testing at virological failure was not available for all participants and stored plasma was not always available for retrospective sequencing.

The investigators could not quantify adherence using pharmacologic measurements or proportion of days covered, despite hypothesizing that suboptimal adherence was an important cause of virological failure.
The authors concluded that B/F/TAF produced high rates of virological suppression, particularly when used as a switch strategy in people with suppressed viraemia.
The authors recommended considering close HIV-1 RNA monitoring in unsuppressed patients with previous therapeutic failure and pre-existing resistance mutations.
The authors concluded that virological failure was rarely associated with selection of resistance mutations and that most participants achieved viral-load re-suppression after a failure.
